newsitem.title: DENMARK: European ministers plan joint air traffic control.
newsitem.headline: European ministers plan joint air traffic control.

text.p: Traffic Ministers from 35 countries met in the Danish capital on Friday in a first step toward building a unified system of European air traffic control, independent TV2 reported.

The ministers, from countries belonging to the European Civil Aviation Conference, discussed a proposal that future decisions on co-operation in air safety and traffic control be taken at Eurocontrol, the European air safety organisation.
"It's about getting as many countries as possible to create a system with which we can work together," Danish Transport Minister Bjoern Westh told TV2.
The television said that the initiative sought to deal with growing congestion in European skies and an increasing number of flight delays, which have doubled in the past year.
It did not report any firm decisions. --Steve Weizman, Copenhagen newsroom +45 33969650
